data.title: Frasers Property Treasury Issues S$40 Million Notes to Extend Debt Maturities
data.description:
An announcement from Frasers Property ( (SG:TQ5) ) is now available.

Frasers Property Treasury Pte. Ltd., a financing arm of Singapore’s Frasers Property Limited, operates a S$5 billion multicurrency debt issuance programme to support the group’s real estate portfolio and related investments. The issuer’s notes are guaranteed by the parent, enhancing credit strength and market access for its capital-raising activities.

The company has issued S$40 million of 3.50% fixed rate notes due 2037 under Series 007, comprising S$1.75 million in additional notes and S$38.25 million in new notes arising from an invitation to existing noteholders. Following the purchase and cancellation of some existing 4.15% notes due 2027, S$442 million of those notes remain outstanding, while the new Series 007 notes are slated for listing on the Singapore Exchange, refining the group’s debt profile and extending its maturity ladder.

data.title: Cloudbreak Pharma Shares Suspended in Hong Kong Amid IPO Manipulation Probe
data.description:
Cloudbreak Pharma, Inc. ( (HK:2592) ) just unveiled an update.

Cloudbreak Pharma has had trading in its shares suspended on the Hong Kong Stock Exchange following a directive from the Securities and Futures Commission, which is probing whether the company’s initial public offering was manipulated to create an artificial impression of investor demand. The regulator says the halt is needed to maintain an orderly and fair market and protect investors while its investigation continues, with Cloudbreak seeking legal advice, pledging full cooperation, and stressing that its business operations remain normal despite the suspension.

All dealings in Cloudbreak Pharma’s shares have been halted since 9:00 a.m. on 10 September 2026 and will remain suspended until further notice from the authorities. The company has urged shareholders and potential investors to exercise caution regarding its securities as the investigation proceeds and further announcements are awaited.

data.title: ADM Energy Secures Adjournment in HMRC Winding-Up Case as AIM Suspension Persists
data.description:
ADM Energy plc ( (GB:ADME) ) has provided an announcement.

ADM Energy PLC, the natural resources investor with oil and gas interests in the U.S. and offshore Nigeria, has provided an update on the winding-up petition brought by the U.K. tax authority. The company continues to derive exposure to upstream hydrocarbons through stakes in Vega Oil and Gas, Eco Oil, OFX Technologies and the Aje Field, positioning it as a niche player in higher-risk, asset-backed energy investments.

The second court hearing of the HMRC winding-up petition on 16 September 2026 resulted in a 42-day adjournment, with the case relisted for 28 October 2026 and no winding-up order made to date. Trading in ADM’s shares remains suspended from AIM pending publication of its 2025 annual report and accounts, leaving investors and creditors focused on the outcome of the rescheduled hearing and the company’s ability to regularise its financial reporting and resolve its dispute with the tax authority.

data.title: Gremi Media Restructures Credit Line with ING Bank Śląski
data.description:
An update from Gremi Media SA ( (PL:GME) ) is now available.

Gremi Media S.A. has amended its long-standing multiproduct agreement with ING Bank Śląski, reducing the overall credit limit to PLN 1.1 million and narrowing the scope of the facility to bank guarantees only. The term of these guarantees has been extended to late July 2028, with collateral simplified to a single blank promissory note and related declaration, signaling a more streamlined and potentially lower-risk financing structure for the company and its banking partner.

The adjustment of the credit limit and focus on guarantees suggests Gremi Media is aligning its banking facilities more tightly with current operational needs and risk management policies. For stakeholders, the move indicates a controlled and structured approach to leverage, potentially improving transparency and predictability of the company’s financial obligations while maintaining access to essential guarantee instruments for its business activities.
